title: Can I BEAT Ancient Chess? (Chaturanga)
summary: Chaturanga (ancient chess) on chess.com: elephants leap exactly two squares diagonally, the counselor (ferz) moves one square diagonally, chariots are rooks, pawns move one square only (no double step, no en passant), no castling. Game 1 is won by abandonment, he wins another and the final long game is a draw.
rules: Elephant: jumps exactly 2 squares diagonally (can jump over a piece).
Chariot = rook, horse = knight, king normal but no castling.
Pawns move 1 square only (no double step, no en passant); promote (to counselor in classical rules - chess.com shows promotion at 23:10).
win_condition: Checkmate (also bare king per chess.com rules - inferred).
